run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/fraud-detection since 2026-11-15T11:35:27Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/fraud-detection is explained by error status on fraud-detection's client spans to its feature-flag dependency flagd, not by failing order processing. In this Prometheus the only request-level series carrying service_name=fraud-detection are the spanmetrics family, and the only STATUS_CODE_ERROR series for that service in the incident window are flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream (one per pod, 10 pods) and flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveInt (2 pods). Jaeger shows those EventStream client spans lasting ~594–602 s and ending with error=true, otel.status_code=ERROR, rpc.grpc.status_code=4 (DEADLINE_EXCEEDED); the child flagd server span in trace bd06756e0c7d97b40a884e5dac7ffd05 carries otel.status_description "stream closed due to server-side timeout". At 11:00 the cumulative span counters for the service were 12 error spans (10 EventStream + 2 ResolveInt) against 457 non-error spans (469 total), i.e. ratio 0.0256, the same order as the alerted value 0.0222, so the alert reading is consistent with these flagd client-span errors still being inside its evaluation window. The service itself looks healthy on its own operational signals: all 10 fraud-detection pods are Running/ready with 0 restarts, the deployment reports 10/10 ready/available, and its application log lines are successful Kafka order consumptions. A separate, unrelated error burst exists at checkout/frontend (PlaceOrder HTTP 500 caused by "shipping quote failure: … Post \"http://shipping:8080/get-quote\": EOF" at 10:55:22), which does not touch fraud-detection spans and is rejected as the cause of this alert.

claims.text: The only metric series in this Prometheus that carry service_name=fraud-detection are traces_span_metrics_calls_total and traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket, and a broad metric-name listing of the window contains no http_server_request_duration_seconds_count, rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_* or app_payment_transactions_total series, so any error-rate reading for this service must come from spanmetrics.

Every STATUS_CODE_ERROR spanmetric series for service_name=fraud-detection is a SPAN_KIND_CLIENT span on span_name flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream (10 series, one per exported pod instance, each with cumulative value 1 sampled at 11:36:03, 11:41:03 and 11:46:03) or on flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveInt (2 series with value 1), with no error series on any other operation.

At 11:00:00 the fraud-detection span counters summed to 12 error spans (EventStream STATUS_CODE_ERROR = 10, ResolveInt STATUS_CODE_ERROR = 2) and 457 non-error spans (orders process STATUS_CODE_UNSET = 230, orders receive STATUS_CODE_UNSET = 221, resolve STATUS_CODE_UNSET = 4, ResolveInt STATUS_CODE_UNSET = 2), i.e. 469 spans total and an error ratio of 12/469 = 0.0256, the same order as the alert's stated 0.0222.

Jaeger returns fraud-detection spans with error=true on operation flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream only: 10 spans, all error_rows=10, each status {"error":true,"otel.status_code":"ERROR","rpc.grpc.status_code":"4"}, with durations 594,101,234–601,796,702 µs and start times from 2026-11-15T10:44:04Z to about 10:54Z.

Trace bd06756e0c7d97b40a884e5dac7ffd05 contains exactly two spans: the fraud-detection EventStream client span 98b55d8661c53e21 (599,999,905 µs, error=true, rpc.grpc.status_code=4) and, referenced as its CHILD_OF parent, the flagd (service flagd, v0.12.8) server span 7a4ab60e782bfb14 (553,397,947 µs, rpc.grpc.status_code=4) whose only error detail is otel.status_description "stream closed due to server-side timeout".

On the dependency side, service flagd records its own error spans on flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream in this window (5 rows, durations 532,498,814–553,397,947 µs, status rpc.grpc.status_code=4) each carrying the status description "stream closed due to server-side timeout"; the same operation also shows 3 error spans attributed to service ad (599,998–604,202 ms, status 4), so the stream closure is a flagd-side behaviour seen by more than one client of that dependency.

fraud-detection itself is up and its workload is fully available: deployment fraud-detection (created 2026-11-15T10:39:27Z, image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-fraud-detection) reports replicas 10, ready 10, available 10, updated 10 with Available=True and NewReplicaSetAvailable=True; ReplicaSet fraud-detection-9fb7d885b (created 10:39:28Z) has 10 ready pods, and all 10 pods (created 10:39:29Z–10:42:32Z) are Running with ready=true and restartCount 0 and no last-termination reason.

The application log lines read from pod fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-486vl between 2026-11-15T10:52:13Z and 10:56:40Z (108 lines, newest 100 shown) are all "Consumed record with orderId: …, and updated total count to: N" Kafka consumption messages; no error, exception or flagd-related line appears in that visible span of stdout.

A Jaeger sample of 40 fraud-detection traces in the window returned 80 spans, all operation "orders receive" (40) and "orders process" (40) with status_state not_recorded and error_rows 0, and business span durations of 427–938 µs for "orders process" and 1,913–99,111 µs for "orders receive"; no failing order-handling span was observed.

A change occurred on the flagd deployment inside the window: a new ReplicaSet flagd-58db7486bd was created at 2026-11-15T10:41:21Z with 1 ready replica while the earlier ReplicaSet flagd-c47676d99 (created 10:39:28Z) was left with 0 replicas, and the current flagd pod flagd-58db7486bd-2plsx (created 10:41:21Z) is Running/ready with restartCount 0 for both containers; no event mentioning flagd or fraud-detection was returned for the window.

fraud-detection's own request handling shows no failure evidence: its order spans carry no error status, its pods are all ready with zero restarts, and its logs show successful order consumption, so the alerted error rate is not accompanied by observed failed fraud-check requests in the spans or logs that were visible.

The checkout HTTP 500 burst is not the source of fraud-detection's error rate: the one checkout error trace in the window (start 2026-11-15T10:55:22Z) fails with rpc.grpc.status_code=13 and otel.status_description "shipping quote failure: failed POST to shipping service: Post \"http://shipping:8080/get-quote\": EOF" on checkout/frontend/frontend-proxy/load-generator spans, and its only fraud-detection-free dependency chain involves shipping, not fraud-detection; that trace contains no fraud-detection span at all.

fraud-detection pod crashes, restarts or evictions are not the cause: all 10 pods are Running and ready with restartCount 0 and no last-termination reason/OOMKilled/Evicted marker, and no event for fraud-detection or flagd was returned in the window, so the error spans cannot be attributed to container restarts.

The alert value 0.0222 is consistent with the spanmetrics error ratio for fraud-detection: 10 EventStream client error spans plus 2 ResolveInt error spans against roughly 540 service spans, i.e. the 12 error spans recorded when the ~600 s EventStream calls terminated (≈10:54–11:04Z) were still inside a ~1 h evaluation window when the alert fired at 11:35:27Z; the exact rule expression, window and threshold could not be read.

The deepest supported cause is the flagd dependency closing the long-lived flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream after roughly 9–10 minutes (server-side status description "stream closed due to server-side timeout"), which lands on the clients as gRPC code 4 with a 600 s deadline and is recorded as an ERROR client span on each fraud-detection pod; the same stream-closure error text also appears on service ad's EventStream spans, indicating a shared flagd-side behaviour rather than a fraud-detection-only defect.

Whether the 10:41:21Z flagd ReplicaSet replacement contributed to the stream closures is unresolved: the erroring EventStream client spans all start at 10:44:04Z or later, i.e. after the new flagd pod flagd-58db7486bd-2plsx was running (created 10:41:21Z, no restarts), so a simple connection reset by that rollout does not by itself explain timeouts that begin on post-rollout streams; no configuration change record is available to test this.

Retrieve and inspect the RequestErrorRate rule definition (evaluation window, denominator, and whether SPAN_KIND_CLIENT spans are counted) from the alerting rule files that back this Alertmanager, because the Prometheus rules API in this target returned no alerting rules and the expression could not be read here.

Treat long-lived streaming spans (flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream, ~600 s duration) as non-request spans in the error-rate SLI, or align the fraud-detection flagd gRPC deadline with flagd's server-side stream timeout and keepalive settings, since the current SLI counts a normal stream re-establishment as an error and makes any single such event raise the ratio above zero.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate alerting rule itself could not be read: list_prometheus_rules returned no_data both for rule_name=RequestErrorRate and for type=alert, so the rule expression, evaluation window, denominator and threshold are unknown and the alert's 0.0222 value could only be reconciled by arithmetic inference.

Spanmetrics data in this Prometheus is sparse and irregularly sampled: an instant query for any fraud-detection series at 11:35:27Z returned no_data, the per-pod error counters are visible only at 11:36:03/11:41:03/11:46:03, and counter values drop between samples (e.g. fraud-detection error total 12 at 11:00–11:05 then 5 at 11:06), so the exact rate at alert time and any increase after ~11:06 could not be measured.

No baseline before the incident window exists for these series: the spanmetric counters only start with the pods created at 10:39:29Z–10:42:32Z, and queries extending back to 2026-11-14 returned no earlier samples, so it cannot be determined whether flagd EventStream timeouts are new since the 10:39–10:41 deployments or a recurring behaviour.

Observability after ~10:56Z is missing: application log lines end at 10:56:40Z, Jaeger samples end at ~10:59Z, and metric samples thin out after ~11:06–11:13Z, so whether further EventStream timeouts occurred between ~11:04Z and the alert at 11:35:27Z is unknown.

The two flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveInt error spans (one on each of two pods) have no corresponding trace in Jaeger (search for that operation with error=true returned no result) and no error detail, so their exact cause and whether they share the stream-timeout cause is unverified.

flagd's configured stream timeout/keepalive could not be verified: the only flagd configmap in the namespace is flagd-config containing demo.flagd.json, with no readable timeout setting, and secrets cannot be read.
The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so no record of the fraud-detection/flagd configuration change behind the 10:39–10:41 ReplicaSet replacements exists in evidence.

Kubernetes-state metric series (e.g. kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready, kube_replicaset_owner) returned no series in this Prometheus, so workload status had to be read from the Kubernetes API at query time rather than as a time series across the window.
next_steps: Inspect the alerting rule source for RequestErrorRate to confirm its window, denominator and whether SPAN_KIND_CLIENT streaming spans are counted.

Compare flagd's server-side EventStream timeout/keepalive configuration with the fraud-detection client's 600 s gRPC deadline, and decide whether the timeout-induced stream close should be classified as an error.
Collect spanmetrics for fraud-detection over several hours to determine whether one flagd EventStream timeout per pod recurs every ~10 minutes or was a one-off after the 10:39–10:41 pod replacements.

Review the separate checkout/shipping failure at 10:55:22Z ("Post http://shipping:8080/get-quote: EOF") under its own alert, since it affects checkout, frontend and frontend-proxy but not fraud-detection.
